title: Sidney’s Arcadia
html_source: The Countess of Pembroke’s Arcadia, also known simply as the Arcadia, is a long prose work by Sir Philip Sidney written towards the end of the 16th century. The source of the subplot in Shakespeare’s King Lear involving Gloucester, Edgar, and Edmund is a tale in the Arcadia with a blind Paphlagonian king and his two sons, Leonatus and Plexitrus.
